name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,733

clue.text: Spooner's cooked food that's on the breakfast table

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so his version of a phrase trades its initial consonants

blocks.note: roast means cooked and tack is food, as in the sailor's hardtack; swap the R and T sounds

explanation.surface: Someone describes a cooked dish waiting on the breakfast table.
explanation.walkthrough: Tack is an old word for food, best known from hardtack, the ship's biscuit. Swapping the opening sounds of ROAST TACK gives TOAST RACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast rack is the slotted holder that keeps slices of toast upright beside the butter and marmalade at breakfast.

clue.text: Now, this sometimes supersedes his spoken word of reassurance

indicators.note: what is spoken is heard rather than read, so the answer only has to share a sound with the clued term

blocks.note: 'there, there' is what you say to comfort someone

explanation.surface: A comment on modern usage, where a once-standard pronoun is giving way to another in speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description: in gender-neutral writing today, THEIR often replaces 'his' ("everyone took their seat").
explanation.definitionFit: Singular possessive they is now widely used where older grammar insisted on a masculine pronoun for an unspecified person.

clue.text: Steamer I caught, taking passage to New World

indicators.note: a passage is a stretch of text, so we take a run of consecutive letters straight out of the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words, ignoring the gaps

explanation.surface: An emigrant boards a steamship to cross the Atlantic for a new life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking passage' reads as booking a berth on a ship; here it means taking a passage of text.
explanation.definitionFit: The New World is the traditional European name for the Americas, discovered by Europeans after the Old World.

clue.text: Turn up house temperature to get by

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up flips it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
T is the standard abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Advice to crank up the heating in your home just to cope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get by' looks like the phrase meaning cope, but 'by' stands alone as the definition. A semi is a semi-detached house, a British staple.
explanation.definitionFit: In multiplication and measurements, 'three by four' and 'three times four' mean the same product, so the two words interchange.

clue.text: Caber one tossed outside circle, as form of exercise

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; 'aerobic' is also used as shorthand for aerobic exercise

indicators.note: something tossed is thrown about, so its letters land in a fresh order
one thing placed outside another wraps around it

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Tossing the caber, the Highland Games event, is presented as a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: A caber is the long tree trunk thrown at Scottish Highland Games, and 'tossed' fits it naturally. Shuffle CABER and I around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobic workouts such as running or dance classes raise breathing and heart rate, and the word names that style of training.

clue.text: Film released after treatment for Kevin Spacey's beginning

indicators.note: to give something treatment is to work on it, so these letters are processed into a new order
a beginning is the opening, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written
the initial of the actor's surname
released means let out

explanation.surface: A film about an actor's return after treatment, alluding to Kevin Spacey's troubled career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is a placement instruction: the released part follows the rearranged name and initial. The film is the 2019 whodunnit starring Daniel Craig.
explanation.definitionFit: Knives Out is a 2019 murder-mystery movie by Rian Johnson, so it is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Came to like The Guardian

blocks.note: first meaning: regained consciousness, past tense of wake
second meaning: alert to social injustice, a label often pinned on that left-leaning paper

explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is a British left-of-centre newspaper whose critics call it woke; 'came to' is the past tense of waking up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of wake, meaning regained consciousness, and a slang adjective for socially progressive views.

clue.text: Owen, chest bared, should get girls

indicators.note: stripping the outer covering exposes what lies inside, so only the inner letters of the words remain

blocks.note: drop the first and last letters of the pair of words

explanation.surface: A man named Owen is told that baring his chest will attract women.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outer letters from 'Owen, chest' and the inside reads WENCHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Wench is an old-fashioned, now jocular word for a young woman or serving girl, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Cat reportedly on track of bird

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a sound rather than a spelling

blocks.note: kitty is a pet name for a cat
a wake is the track left behind a ship

explanation.surface: A cat stalks a bird by following its trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the second part after the first in a down entry. A wake is the trail of disturbed water behind a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull of northern seas, named after its call, so it is a kind of seabird.

clue.text: Soldiers consider queen a saviour

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to deem is to consider or judge
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Troops regard their monarch as the one who rescued them.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers and ER for Elizabeth Regina, both stock abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Redeemer is a title for one who rescues or delivers others, especially Christ in Christian worship.

clue.text: News at Ten - viewing only middle bit with Brunel is essential

indicators.note: watching just the middle portion means keeping only the central letter of a word

blocks.note: Brunel is the setter, who refers to themself as I
N is short for new, so news is read as more than one N
taken as written
the centre of the three-letter word

explanation.surface: The setter claims that half-watching the ITV evening bulletin is a vital part of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: News at Ten is a British TV news programme; here it splits into its words. The setter's own pseudonym stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate qualities are inborn and inherent, part of a thing's basic nature, which is what essential means here.

clue.text: They're typically round gold coins

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
bits are small coins, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A remark that gold coins are usually circular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round gold coins' reads as one phrase, but 'round' belongs to the definition. A threepenny bit was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetary paths are roughly circular or elliptical, so the definition describes them by their usual shape.

clue.text: Mingle briefly with one's ambassador in front of Palace

indicators.note: doing something briefly cuts it short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: blend, meaning mingle, without its last letter
His Excellency, an ambassador's title
one is I, and 'one's' is read as I'M

explanation.surface: Briefly socialising with your country's ambassador outside a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is the contraction 'one is', so with one as I it becomes I'M. HE (His Excellency) is the form of address for an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Blenheim Palace in Oxfordshire is the stately home where Winston Churchill was born, so it names a particular palace.

clue.text: Protective cover helps heat house centrally

indicators.note: what sits centrally lies in the middle, so the letters are found inside the words

blocks.note: the run starts at the end of the first word and ends at the start of the third

explanation.surface: Insulation that helps keep the warmth in the middle of a home.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of 'helps', all of 'heat' and the start of 'house'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting case, such as one for a knife blade or an electric cable, that guards what it holds.

clue.text: One making pointed attack on individuals in school?

definitions.text: One making pointed attack on individuals in school?

blocks.clueFragment: One making pointed attack on individuals in school?
blocks.note: surface reading: a bully making barbed remarks at particular pupils

blocks.clueFragment: pointed attack on individuals in school
blocks.note: setter's reading: a whaler spearing members of a school of whales

explanation.walkthrough: A school is also a group of whales or fish, and the pointed attack is a spear thrown from a whaling boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpooner throws or fires the barbed spear used in whaling, striking particular animals within a group at sea.

clue.text: Cycling onwards ultimately dissipated upper body pains

indicators.note: cycling sends something round in a loop, so the front letter moves to the back
the final part has evaporated, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: going onwards is going ahead
the chest, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A cyclist pushes on and the upper-body aches fade away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper body pains' looks like the definition, but 'upper body' is the chest and 'pains' alone defines. Move the A of AHEAD to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Headaches are specific aches in the head, so they are a kind of pain; the plural fits too.

clue.text: Centred ball leads to save - bringing this into play?

definitions.text: Centred ball leads to save - bringing this into play?

blocks.note: a cross is a ball centred from the wing in football
save and bar both mean except

explanation.surface: A football commentary: a cross comes in, the keeper tips it away, and the woodwork comes into play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a goalkeeper's stop, but it means except, as does BAR. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The horizontal beam on top of the goalposts often gets involved when a keeper tips a dangerous centre over.

clue.text: Unopened load - mixed tuna and octopus

indicators.note: if something is not opened, its front stays shut away, so the first letter goes
mixing stirs things up, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: cargo, a load, without its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's delivery arrives sealed: a jumble of tuna and octopus.
explanation.walkthrough: The argonaut, or paper nautilus, is a lesser-known octopus; its name also recalls Jason's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The argonaut is a small ocean-going cephalopod whose female grows a papery shell, a genuine member of the octopus order.

clue.text: Tory steps occasionally upset residents in Beds

indicators.note: doing something occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is kept
upsetting things knocks them over and out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Conservative policy moves annoy voters in Bedfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Beds is the usual abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county, but here it means oyster beds on the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters grow in colonies on the sea floor called oyster beds, so they live in such places.

clue.text: Crossing Cook Strait north

indicators.note: to cook something is to work it into a new form, as in cooking the books

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Sailing northward across the Cook Strait between New Zealand's two islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Cook Strait is a real channel in New Zealand, so 'Cook' reads as a name, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing across or through from one side to the other, the same as a crossing.

clue.text: Retro container with an old-fashioned lid

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the letters are read back to front

blocks.note: a pot is a container
'two pounds an hour' means two pounds per hour

explanation.surface: A vintage storage jar comes with an antique-style cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lid' looks like the cover of the container, but it is slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lid is slang for a hat, and a topper is a top hat, a tall formal style rarely worn now.

clue.text: Oxygen pipe I'm assembling to reach where many lie entrapped

indicators.note: assembling means putting parts together, so the letters are built into a new arrangement

blocks.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A rescuer assembles an air line to reach people trapped after a collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: The rescue scene hides a historical one: the trapped victims are those caught by Vesuvius.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman town was buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79, and casts of its victims remain preserved in ash.

clue.text: Seaman leaving India and having first a transfer to Far East country

indicators.note: whatever is leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out

indicators.text: first a transfer to Far East
indicators.note: in an across entry the east is the right-hand end, so the earliest A in the word moves to the far end

blocks.note: a boatswain is a ship's officer in charge of equipment
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A sailor quits India and is posted to the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far East' suggests Asia, but it means the far right of the word. Remove the I, then move the first A to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked nation in southern Africa, so it is a country, despite the Asian hint in the surface.

clue.text: Lean on westbound Asians

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west means running right to left, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: lean and slim both mean thin
on and at both locate, as in 'at the table'

explanation.surface: A call to rely on Asian travellers heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean on' looks like one phrasal verb, but the words split into thin and at.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are a people of southern India and Sri Lanka, so they are a group of South Asians.

clue.text: Mark II?

blocks.note: surface reading: the second version of a car or machine
setter's reading: the Roman two is an old word for two, the surname of the American author named Mark

explanation.walkthrough: Mark II looks like a model number, but II is two, and the archaic word for two is the pen name of the author of Tom Sawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Clemens wrote as Mark Twain, and twain is an old poetic word for two, the value of the Roman numeral.

clue.text: Small animal decapitated by large rat

indicators.note: losing the head means losing the first letter

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
a mouse without its first letter

explanation.surface: A mouse is beheaded by a big rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like the killer in the scene, but it is the definition: a contemptible person. 'By' places L beside the beheaded mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are insults for a despicable, untrustworthy person, so calling someone a rat or a louse means the same.

clue.text: Get stuck in men's pants - what about that!

definitions.note: the answer is transitive: to make something get stuck in a net

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be reordered
one thing going about another wraps round it

blocks.note: 'eh?' is a way of saying 'what?'
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A cheeky exclamation about something caught in a man's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pants are underpants, and 'pants' is also slang for rubbish, which makes it an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To enmesh is to entangle or trap something in a net, so it ends up caught fast in the mesh.

clue.text: Shocked by jokes about eating fish

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
whatever eats something takes it inside itself

blocks.note: puns are jokes on words
a hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by jokes told over a fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' does double duty in feel only: here it turns the jokes round, while 'eating' puts the fish inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shaken up means being upset or disturbed by an event, the same as being shocked.

clue.text: Recall Egypt's principal deity - Sun God

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters come back the other way
the principal part is the chief or first, so only the initial letter is kept

blocks.note: the initial letter of the country
Ra was the chief Egyptian god
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: Remembering Egypt's chief deity, the sun god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun God' reads as one title for Ra, but it splits: S, then the definition. Ra supplies the deity instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek god of war, a member of the Olympian pantheon, so he is one of the gods.

clue.text: It's one finally going free, travelling light

indicators.note: when the end goes, the word loses its final letter
things travelling move about, so the letters end up rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
the word without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is finally released and travels with little luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling light' is a ready-made phrase, but 'light' is the definition, a verb meaning to kindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire or candle is to make it burn, which is exactly what setting something ablaze does.
